story.iWant: I want the application to be fully functional and visually appealing on various screen sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop),
story.soThat: So that I can access my study materials and tools from any device.
story.tasks: - [ ] **Implement Responsive Layouts (AC: 1)** - [ ] Review existing Story 5.1 UI components for responsiveness requirements. - [ ] Apply Tailwind CSS responsive utilities (`sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`) to ensure graceful layout adjustments for all user-facing screens. - [ ] Verify interactive elements (buttons, forms, navigation) remain accessible and usable across mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints. - [ ] **Ensure Cross-Browser Compatibility (AC: 2)** - [ ] Conduct functional testing of the application on the latest stable versions of Chrome, Edge, and Safari. - [ ] Identify and resolve any browser-specific rendering issues or functional discrepancies. - [ ] **Testing & Quality Assurance** - [ ] Perform manual responsive testing on various device emulators (e.g., Chrome DevTools device mode) for common mobile and tablet sizes. - [ ] Conduct manual responsive testing on actual mobile phones and tablets. - [ ] Perform manual cross-browser testing for layout and functionality on target browsers. - [ ] Implement visual regression tests for critical responsive layouts to detect unintended changes across breakpoints.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** any user-facing screen **When** viewed on a mobile phone, tablet, or desktop browser **Then** the layout adjusts gracefully, and all interactive elements remain accessible and usable. 2. **And** the application functions correctly on the latest stable versions of Chrome, Edge, and Safari.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The system shall be a Single Page Application (SPA) that is mobile-responsive and functions across target browsers (Chrome, Edge, Safari). ... The UI adapts gracefully to various screen sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop).

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The system shall incorporate core accessibility features, including WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance, strong screen-reader support, and reduced-motion options.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The AI Study Buddy's user experience should embody a supportive, easy/simple, and playful feel. The overall aesthetic will be academic, friendly, and clean, designed to reduce cognitive load and foster a sense of calm and control.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: The AI Study Buddy will adhere to WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance as a baseline. Beyond standard compliance, we will prioritize cognitive accessibility... Strong screen-reader support... Reduced-motion options.

doc.title: AI Study Buddy - High-Level Architecture
doc.snippet: The frontend is a single-page application built with React and Next.js, styled with Tailwind CSS. It communicates with the Supabase backend for data, authentication, and storage, and with the Vercel Function for AI-powered features.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: Ensure the application is intuitive, accessible, and enjoyable to use, fulfilling the promise of a clean, supportive, and frustration-free experience.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Story 5.1: Implement Core UI Design System
doc.snippet: As a Developer, I want to implement the core UI design system based on Tailwind CSS and our UX principles, So that all user-facing components have a consistent, clean, and friendly aesthetic.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Story 5.3: Implement WCAG AA & Screen Reader Support
doc.snippet: As a user with disabilities, I want to use the application effectively with assistive technologies like screen readers, So that I can have an inclusive and equitable learning experience.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: As a user sensitive to motion, I want to minimize animations and transitions in the application, So that I can use the tool comfortably without discomfort.
